contract_review_result.summary: Contract is close, but has one semantic conflict and one missing executable rule that can cause inconsistent implementations around same-cycle dequeue/enqueue behavior.

findings.issue: States simultaneous dequeue/enqueue in FULL is architecturally forbidden and in_ready=0 for whole cycle when FULL at cycle start, even if out_ready=1. This conflicts with the user requirement of one-cycle latency without stalls (in steady no-backpressure operation, this rule injects bubbles and reduces throughput).
findings.requested_change: Revise control and latency semantics to allow same-edge dequeue/enqueue when FULL and out_ready=1 (or explicitly justify and update user-level requirement if throughput is intentionally limited). Ensure rule is consistent across control, pipeline stall_behavior, interface backpressure text, and latency model.

findings.issue: Reset behavior says output register content is don't-care while also requiring deterministic behavior; no explicit post-reset value rule for out_sum when out_valid=0. This can create ambiguity for verification and RTL style checks.
findings.requested_change: Add an explicit executable rule: either (a) out_sum is unconstrained when out_valid=0, or (b) out_sum is driven to a defined reset value (e.g., 0). Keep this consistent in reset section, signal semantics, and acceptance checks.
